statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Intoxicating Liquor or Drugs
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second within 7 years); Class A Misdemeanor (third within 7 years); Class C Felony (fourth+ within 15 years)
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
On a highway or on public or private areas to which the public has a right of access
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor, drugs, or a combination
Or had a BAC of .08 or higher
mandatory_minimum: Addiction evaluation required for all offenses
enhancements: Fourth or subsequent offense within 15 years (Class C Felony)
Refusal to submit to chemical test (additional license suspension)
notes: Implied consent under § 39-20-01. Admin license suspension 91 days first offense. 24/7 sobriety program may be ordered. Look-back period is 7 years for misdemeanor enhancement and 15 years for felony enhancement.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
No prior DUI convictions within 7 years
enhancements: BAC .16 or higher (mandatory 4 days imprisonment or 10 days community service)
notes: Eligible for temporary restricted license after 30 days. Must complete addiction evaluation and any recommended treatment.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (second/third within 7 years); Class C Felony (fourth+ within 15 years)
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment of driving ability
One or more prior DUI convictions within the look-back period
mandatory_minimum: 10 days imprisonment (second); 120 days (third); 1 year and 1 day (fourth+)
notes: Second offense: 365-day license suspension. Third offense: 2-year suspension. Fourth+: 3-year suspension. 24/7 sobriety program mandatory for repeat offenders.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of any drug or substance
Or under the combined influence of alcohol and any drug or substance
To a degree rendering the defendant incapable of safely driving
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
Presence of Schedule I or II substance
notes: No per se limit for drugs. Prosecution must prove actual impairment. Includes legally prescribed medications if they impair driving. Blood or urine test may be required under implied consent.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. Adds points to driving record. May result in license suspension if accumulated points exceed threshold.

statute_title: Leaving the Scene of an Accident — Injury or Death
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (injury); Class C Felony (death or serious injury)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to immediately stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide name, address, and vehicle registration and render reasonable assistance
notes: Leaving scene with property damage only is an infraction under § 39-08-05. Must report accident to law enforcement if injury or death is involved.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant drove or was in actual physical control of a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances
Defendant's conduct caused the death of another person
notes: DUI-related deaths may be charged as manslaughter under § 12.1-16-02 or negligent homicide under § 12.1-16-03. Prosecution must prove causal link between intoxication and death.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By criminal negligence
While operating a motor vehicle
notes: North Dakota does not have a separate vehicular manslaughter statute. Vehicular deaths charged as negligent homicide (Class C Felony) or manslaughter (Class B Felony) depending on culpability.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended, Revoked, or Canceled
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (subsequent)
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a highway
Defendant's license was suspended, revoked, or canceled
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension, revocation, or cancellation
notes: Additional suspension period added. If original suspension was DUI-related, penalties may be enhanced.

statute_title: Fleeing or Attempting to Elude a Police Officer
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (basic); Class C Felony (if endangerment, injury, or death)
elements: A peace officer signaled the defendant to stop
Signal was given by hand, voice, siren, or light
Defendant willfully failed to stop or attempted to flee
The officer was in uniform or an identifiable police vehicle
enhancements: Serious bodily injury results (Class C Felony)
notes: Fleeing that endangers others or causes injury is elevated to a felony. License suspension mandatory upon conviction.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (Schedule IV-V); Class C Felony (Schedule I-III)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed
A controlled substance
Without a valid prescription or legal authorization
notes: North Dakota classifies controlled substances into Schedules I-V. Personal-use amounts may be eligible for deferred imposition of sentence.

offense_class: Infraction (half ounce or less); Class B Misdemeanor (half ounce to one ounce); Class A Misdemeanor (over one ounce)
penalty_max: $1,000 fine only (half ounce or less); 30 days (half ounce to one ounce); 1 year (over one ounce)
fine_max: $1,000 (half ounce or less); $1,500 (half ounce to one ounce); $3,000 (over one ounce)
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed
Marijuana or marijuana concentrate
Without legal authorization
notes: Half ounce or less decriminalized to an infraction in 2019. Medical marijuana legal under Chapter 19-24.1. Concentrate may be charged differently than plant material.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed
Cocaine or crack cocaine (Schedule II)
Without a valid prescription
notes: Cocaine is Schedule II. Possession of any amount is a Class C Felony. Amounts over certain thresholds may support intent-to-deliver charges.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly or intentionally possessed
Methamphetamine (Schedule II)
Without a valid prescription
notes: Methamphetamine is Schedule II. Any amount is a felony. North Dakota has significant meth-related enforcement initiatives.

offense_class: Class A Felony (large quantities); Class B Felony (lesser quantities)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured, delivered, or possessed with intent to deliver
A controlled substance
In a quantity meeting or exceeding trafficking thresholds
mandatory_minimum: 10 years (Class A trafficking); 4 years (Class B trafficking)
notes: Trafficking thresholds vary by substance. Mandatory minimum sentences apply. Asset forfeiture provisions under Chapter 19-03.1.

offense_class: Class B Felony (Schedule I-II); Class C Felony (Schedule III-V)
elements: Defendant knowingly delivered, distributed, or dispensed
A controlled substance
To another person
Without legal authorization
notes: Delivery includes actual, constructive, or attempted transfer. Undercover purchases constitute delivery. Enhanced penalties for delivery to persons under 18.

offense_class: Class B Felony (Schedule I-II); Class C Felony (Schedule III-V)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured, compounded, or processed
A controlled substance
Without legal authorization
enhancements: Manufacturing in presence of a minor
notes: Manufacturing methamphetamine carries additional penalties. Cleanup costs may be assessed. Separate charges for child endangerment if minors present.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly used or possessed with intent to use
Drug paraphernalia

For the purpose of planting, propagating, cultivating, growing, harvesting, manufacturing, compounding, converting, producing, processing, preparing, testing, analyzing, packing, repacking, storing, containing, concealing, injecting, ingesting, inhaling, or otherwise introducing a controlled substance into the body
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Paraphernalia is broadly defined. Delivery of paraphernalia is a Class A Misdemeanor. Delivery to a minor under 18 is a Class C Felony.

offense_class: Class B Felony (Schedule I-II); Class C Felony (Schedule III-V)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
With the intent to manufacture, deliver, or distribute
The intent may be inferred from quantity, packaging, or other evidence
notes: Intent inferred from circumstantial evidence including quantity, packaging, scales, large amounts of cash, and communications. Same penalty as delivery.

offense_class: Class AA Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused the death of another human being
With willfulness, deliberation, and premeditation
notes: North Dakota does not have the death penalty. Class AA Felony carries mandatory life without parole. Only charge classified as Class AA.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally or knowingly caused the death of another human being
Without premeditation
Or caused death during the commission of a felony (felony murder)
enhancements: During commission of specified felonies (robbery, burglary, kidnapping, arson, sexual assault)
notes: Includes felony murder during commission of specified dangerous felonies. Class A Felony carries up to life imprisonment with possibility of parole.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another human being
Under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to the value of human life
Or caused death under the influence of extreme emotional disturbance for which there is reasonable excuse
notes: North Dakota combines what other states call voluntary and involuntary manslaughter into a single manslaughter statute. Extreme emotional disturbance is an affirmative defense that reduces murder to manslaughter.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant negligently caused the death of another human being
notes: North Dakota's equivalent of involuntary manslaughter. Requires criminal negligence, which is a gross deviation from the standard of care that a reasonable person would exercise.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant willfully caused serious bodily injury to another person
Or caused bodily injury with a dangerous weapon, firearm, or destructive device
Or caused bodily injury while attempting to inflict serious bodily injury
enhancements: Victim is a peace officer, firefighter, or emergency medical services personnel
notes: Serious bodily injury means injury creating a substantial risk of death, serious permanent disfigurement, or protracted loss of function of any body part.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (subsequent or against specific victims)
penalty_max: 30 days (first); 1 year (subsequent or against specific victims)
elements: Defendant willfully caused bodily injury to another person
Or negligently caused bodily injury with a dangerous weapon
enhancements: Victim is a peace officer or emergency responder (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Bodily injury means any impairment of physical condition, including physical pain. Assault against certain protected victims is automatically a Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant willfully caused bodily injury to another person
notes: North Dakota does not have a separate battery statute. Offensive touching or bodily harm is prosecuted under simple assault (§ 12.1-17-01).

offense_class: Class B Felony (basic); Class A Felony (if armed or inflicting bodily injury)
elements: Defendant took property from another person or in the person's presence
By force or threat of imminent force
With intent to permanently deprive the owner of the property
enhancements: Armed with a dangerous weapon (Class A Felony)
Infliction of bodily injury (Class A Felony)
notes: Robbery by force or threat without a weapon or injury is a Class B Felony. Use of a weapon or causing injury elevates to Class A Felony.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant committed robbery
While armed with a firearm or other dangerous weapon
Or inflicted or attempted to inflict bodily injury upon another
notes: Armed robbery is the most serious robbery charge. Weapon need not be used — mere possession during robbery is sufficient.

offense_class: Class A Felony (if terrorizing, sexual assault, or ransom); Class B Felony (other kidnapping)
elements: Defendant removed another person from one place to another
Or confined another person for a substantial period
Without the person's consent or the consent of a parent/guardian of a minor
With intent to hold for ransom, terrorize, facilitate commission of a felony, or interfere with a governmental function
notes: Kidnapping involving ransom, terrorizing, or sexual assault is Class A Felony. Unlawful restraint is a lesser included offense under § 12.1-18-03.

offense_class: Class B Felony (occupied structure); Class C Felony (other property)
elements: Defendant intentionally started or maintained a fire or caused an explosion
Damaged a building or occupied structure
The building belonged to another or was insured against fire
enhancements: Occupied structure at time of fire (Class B Felony)
notes: Arson of an occupied structure is Class B Felony. Arson of property is Class C Felony. Reckless arson is a lesser included offense.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant intended to cause the death of another person
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward the commission of murder
enhancements: Victim is a law enforcement officer
notes: Attempted murder is punished one class below the completed offense. Since murder is Class AA, attempted murder is Class A Felony.

statute_title: Aggravated Assault with a Dangerous Weapon
offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant willfully caused bodily injury to another
With a dangerous weapon, firearm, or destructive device
enhancements: Victim is a peace officer or emergency responder
notes: Dangerous weapon includes any instrument capable of causing death or serious bodily injury. Charged under the aggravated assault statute.

offense_class: Class C Felony ($1,000+); Class A Misdemeanor ($250-$999); Class B Misdemeanor (under $250)
elements: Defendant knowingly took or exercised unauthorized control over property of another
With intent to deprive the owner of the property
notes: Value thresholds determine offense class. Aggregation of thefts from same victim over 180 days permitted.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly took or exercised unauthorized control over property of another
Value of property was $1,000 or more
With intent to deprive the owner of the property
enhancements: Theft of a firearm (automatic Class C Felony regardless of value)
notes: North Dakota does not use the term 'grand theft' but theft of property valued $1,000+ is a Class C Felony. Theft exceeding $10,000 is Class B Felony.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly took or exercised unauthorized control over property of another
Value of property was less than $250
With intent to deprive the owner of the property
notes: Theft of property valued $250-$999 is Class A Misdemeanor. Under $250 is Class B Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Same thresholds as general theft
penalty_max: Same as general theft by value
fine_max: Same as general theft by value
elements: Defendant knowingly took possession of merchandise from a retail establishment
Without paying the purchase price
With intent to deprive the merchant of the merchandise
notes: Shoplifting is prosecuted under the general theft statute. Civil demand provisions allow merchants to seek damages under § 51-21-08.1.

offense_class: Class B Felony (dwelling, weapon, or assault); Class C Felony (other structures)
elements: Defendant willfully entered or surreptitiously remained in a building or occupied structure
With intent to commit a crime therein
enhancements: Armed with a dangerous weapon (Class B Felony)
Assault or menacing during burglary (Class B Felony)
notes: Burglary of a dwelling, while armed, or involving assault is automatically Class B Felony regardless of the structure type.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant willfully entered or surreptitiously remained in a dwelling
With intent to commit a crime therein
notes: Dwelling includes any building or structure where a person lives or habitually sleeps. Always classified as Class B Felony.

offense_class: Class C Felony (most vehicles exceed $1,000)
elements: Defendant knowingly took or exercised unauthorized control over a motor vehicle belonging to another
With intent to deprive the owner of the vehicle
notes: Motor vehicle theft is charged under the general theft statute based on value. No separate auto theft statute.

offense_class: Same classification as theft by value
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of property of another
Knowing or having reason to know the property was stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Classified the same as theft based on the value of the property received. Knowledge of stolen status may be inferred from circumstances.

offense_class: Class B Felony (over $10,000 damage); Class C Felony ($2,000-$10,000); Class A Misdemeanor ($100-$2,000); Class B Misdemeanor (under $100)
penalty_max: 10 years (Class B Felony); 5 years (Class C Felony); 1 year (Class A Misd); 30 days (Class B Misd)
fine_max: $20,000 (Class B Felony); $10,000 (Class C Felony); $3,000 (Class A Misd); $1,500 (Class B Misd)
elements: Defendant intentionally or recklessly damaged property of another
Without the owner's consent
notes: Vandalism charged under criminal mischief statute. Offense class depends on dollar amount of damage. Restitution commonly ordered.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (basic); Class A Misdemeanor (dwelling or fenced property)
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully in or upon premises
Notice against trespass was given by posting, fencing, or personal communication
enhancements: Trespass on a dwelling (Class A Misdemeanor)
Trespass on fenced or secured property (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Notice may be by posting signs, fencing, or personal communication. Trespass on a dwelling is automatically Class A Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Varies by damage amount (see vandalism entry)
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged tangible property of another
Or recklessly damaged tangible property of another in the course of committing another offense
notes: Same statute as vandalism. Offense level determined by dollar amount of damage caused.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second within 5 years); Class C Felony (third+ within 5 years)
elements: Defendant willfully caused bodily injury to a family or household member
Or attempted to cause bodily injury to a family or household member
mandatory_minimum: Domestic violence assessment required for all convictions
enhancements: Second offense within 5 years (Class A Misdemeanor)
Third or subsequent within 5 years (Class C Felony)
notes: Family or household member includes spouses, former spouses, persons related by blood/marriage, persons who share a child, and persons living together. Protection orders available under Chapter 14-07.1.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first offense)
elements: Defendant willfully caused bodily injury to a family or household member
enhancements: Prior domestic violence convictions within 5 years
notes: North Dakota does not have a separate domestic battery statute. Domestic physical harm is charged under the domestic violence statute § 12.1-17-01.2.

offense_class: Class C Felony (serious risk); Class A Misdemeanor (general endangerment)
elements: Defendant was a parent, guardian, or caretaker of a child
Defendant knowingly or negligently created a substantial risk of serious bodily injury or death to the child
Or failed to provide necessary care
enhancements: Drug use or manufacturing in presence of child
Leaving child unattended in dangerous circumstances
notes: Includes leaving children in vehicles, exposure to drug manufacturing, and failure to provide medical care. May be charged alongside DUI if child is in the vehicle.

statute_title: Abuse or Neglect of a Child
offense_class: Class C Felony (serious harm); Class A Misdemeanor (lesser harm)
elements: Defendant willfully inflicted bodily injury upon a child
Or subjected a child to cruel treatment or cruel neglect
Defendant was a parent, guardian, or person having custody
enhancements: Serious bodily injury (Class B Felony under § 12.1-17-02)
notes: Serious physical abuse may be charged as aggravated assault. Mandatory reporting requirements under § 50-25.1-03.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: A valid protection order was in effect
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant willfully violated a term of the order
enhancements: Prior violations (Class C Felony for second+ within 2 years)
notes: Second or subsequent violation within 2 years is a Class C Felony. Violation may also result in contempt of court proceedings.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class C Felony (subsequent or with protective order)
elements: Defendant intentionally engaged in a course of conduct
Directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to feel frightened, intimidated, or harassed
Defendant knew or should have known the conduct would cause fear
enhancements: Violation of protection order during stalking (Class C Felony)
notes: Course of conduct means two or more acts over a period of time evidencing a continuity of purpose. Cyberstalking included.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant engaged in conduct directed at a specific person
With intent to frighten, intimidate, or harass
Conduct included following, monitoring, threats, or repeated unwanted contact
notes: Harassment includes repeated unwanted communications, following, and monitoring. Conduct must be directed at a specific individual.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of a Vulnerable Adult
offense_class: Class C Felony (exploitation/serious harm); Class A Misdemeanor (neglect)
elements: Defendant willfully abused, neglected, or exploited a vulnerable adult
Victim was a vulnerable adult as defined by law
Defendant was a caregiver or person in a position of trust
notes: Vulnerable adult includes persons aged 60+ and disabled adults. Financial exploitation is common charge. Mandatory reporting under § 50-25.2-03.

statute_title: Possession of a Firearm or Dangerous Weapon
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general restrictions); Class C Felony (specific prohibitions)
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm or dangerous weapon
Under circumstances prohibited by law
enhancements: Possession at school or public gathering
notes: North Dakota is generally permissive on firearms. Constitutional carry (permitless concealed carry) for residents enacted in 2017. Restrictions apply to prohibited persons, schools, and certain public buildings.

statute_title: Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class C Felony (if violent felony or subsequent)
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant had a prior felony conviction
Felony conviction involved violence or threat of violence, or defendant had not had rights restored
enhancements: Possession during commission of another crime
notes: North Dakota allows firearm rights restoration for certain non-violent felons after 10 years. Violent felons are permanently prohibited. Federal 18 U.S.C. § 922(g) also applies.

statute_title: Carrying a Concealed Firearm or Weapon — Violation
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant carried a concealed firearm or dangerous weapon
In a prohibited location or without meeting statutory requirements
notes: North Dakota enacted constitutional carry in 2017 (HB 1169). Residents may carry concealed without a permit. Non-residents still need a recognized permit. Prohibited locations include schools, courthouses, and secured government buildings.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant willfully or recklessly discharged a firearm
In a manner that endangered the safety of others
notes: Discharge that causes injury may be charged as assault or aggravated assault. Municipal ordinances may impose additional restrictions.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly used or transferred identifying information of another person
Without the person's authorization
With intent to commit or aid in the commission of any unlawful activity
enhancements: Victim is a vulnerable adult or minor
notes: Identifying information includes name, SSN, date of birth, driver's license number, financial account numbers, and biometric data. Restitution commonly ordered.

offense_class: Same classification as theft by value
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property as an agent, employee, or fiduciary
Defendant knowingly converted the property to personal use
Without authorization
notes: North Dakota does not have a separate embezzlement statute. Embezzlement is prosecuted as theft by deception or unauthorized taking under § 12.1-23-02.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant, with intent to defraud or deceive
Falsely made, completed, or altered a written instrument
Or knowingly uttered or possessed a forged instrument
notes: Written instrument includes checks, deeds, contracts, currency, and official documents. Uttering (passing) a forged instrument is the same offense class.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant made or altered an object
So that it appeared to have value because of age, rarity, source, or authorship it did not possess
With intent to defraud
notes: Most currency counterfeiting is prosecuted federally. State charges apply to simulated objects of value. Charged under forgery or criminal simulation statutes.

statute_title: Issuing a Check Without Sufficient Funds
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (under $500); Class A Misdemeanor ($500-$1,000); Class C Felony (over $1,000)
penalty_max: 30 days (Class B); 1 year (Class A); 5 years (Class C Felony)
elements: Defendant issued a check or draft for the payment of money
Knowing at the time of issuance that there were insufficient funds
The check was dishonored upon presentation
notes: Defendant must be given written notice and 10 days to make the check good before prosecution. Payment within that period is a defense.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly presented or caused to be presented
A false or fraudulent claim or statement
To an insurance company
For the purpose of obtaining payment or benefit
notes: Includes auto insurance fraud, health insurance fraud, and property insurance fraud. Restitution and civil penalties may also apply.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly used a credit card, debit card, or account number
Without authorization of the cardholder or issuer
To obtain money, goods, or services
notes: May be charged as theft, identity theft, or both depending on circumstances. Federal charges may also apply for interstate transactions.

offense_class: Class B Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly conducted a financial transaction
Involving proceeds of criminal activity
With intent to promote the carrying on of criminal activity
Or to disguise the nature, source, or ownership of the proceeds
notes: Often charged alongside drug trafficking or fraud offenses. Asset forfeiture provisions apply. Federal charges common for larger amounts.

offense_class: Same classification as theft by value
elements: Defendant obtained property of another by deception
Defendant created or reinforced a false impression of law, value, intention, or other state of mind
With intent to deprive the owner of the property
notes: General fraud is prosecuted as theft by deception under the theft statute. Specific fraud statutes may apply for insurance, securities, or government programs.

offense_class: Class AA Felony (victim under 15); Class A Felony (other circumstances)
elements: Defendant engaged in a sexual act with another person
By compulsion, through threat of imminent death or serious bodily injury
Or the victim was under 15 years of age
Or the victim was incapable of consent due to mental disease, intoxication, or unconsciousness
mandatory_minimum: Life without parole if victim under 15
enhancements: Victim under 15 (Class AA Felony — life without parole)
notes: Gross Sexual Imposition is North Dakota's most serious sexual offense. Lifetime sex offender registration required. Victim under 15 carries mandatory life without parole.

offense_class: Class A Felony
elements: Defendant engaged in a sexual act with another person
By force or threat of force
Without the victim's consent
notes: North Dakota does not use the term 'rape' in its statutes. The equivalent offense is Gross Sexual Imposition (§ 12.1-20-03). Sexual Imposition (§ 12.1-20-04) is a lesser offense.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class C Felony (subsequent)
elements: Defendant exposed genitals or female breast in a public place
With intent to arouse or satisfy sexual desires
Under circumstances in which the defendant knows the conduct is likely to cause affront or alarm
enhancements: Prior conviction for indecent exposure (Class C Felony)
notes: First offense is Class A Misdemeanor. Subsequent conviction is Class C Felony. May require sex offender registration depending on circumstances.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (first); Class C Felony (if involving a minor)
elements: Defendant solicited or hired another person to engage in sexual activity
In exchange for money or other compensation
enhancements: Victim is a minor (Class C Felony)
notes: Promoting prostitution (§ 12.1-29-02) is a separate, more serious offense. Soliciting a minor is a felony. Human trafficking charges may also apply.

offense_class: Class B Felony (production); Class C Felony (possession/distribution)
elements: Defendant knowingly produced, possessed, or distributed
Visual depiction of a minor engaging in sexual conduct
Defendant knew or should have known the person depicted was a minor
notes: Federal charges commonly apply. Production carries more severe penalties than possession. Lifetime sex offender registration required.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant was required to register as a sex offender
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update registration
Within the time period required by law
notes: Registration required for 15 years or lifetime depending on offense. Must verify address annually. Failure to register is a separate felony offense.

offense_class: Class AA Felony (victim under 15); Class A Felony (victim 15-17 with authority figure); Class B Felony (corruption of minor)
penalty_max: Life without parole (under 15); 20 years (Class A); 10 years (Class B)
elements: Defendant engaged in a sexual act or sexual contact with a minor
Victim was below the age of consent
Defendant was the age specified by the applicable statute
mandatory_minimum: Life without parole if victim under 15
enhancements: Position of authority over the victim
notes: Age of consent is 18 in North Dakota. Corruption of a Minor (§ 12.1-20-05) covers sexual contact by adults with 15-17 year olds. Close-in-age exceptions may apply.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant, with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm another person
Engaged in fighting, threatening, or violent behavior
Or made unreasonable noise
Or used abusive or obscene language in a public place
notes: Commonly charged alongside other offenses. Includes disturbing lawful assembly and obstructing traffic.

statute_title: Preventing Arrest or Discharge of Other Duties
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally prevented or attempted to prevent a law enforcement officer
From effecting an arrest or discharging any other official duty
By using or threatening to use physical force or violence
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (Class C Felony)
notes: Physical resistance required — mere refusal to cooperate or verbal objection is not sufficient. Fleeing alone may be charged separately under § 39-10-71.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant intentionally interfered with, obstructed, or hindered
The administration of law or other governmental function
By means of intimidation, force, physical interference, or obstacle
enhancements: Aiding a felony fugitive (Class C Felony)
notes: Includes providing false information to law enforcement, hiding evidence, and harboring fugitives. Aiding a felony suspect elevates the offense.

offense_class: Punitive sanction up to 30 days per count; remedial sanctions until compliance
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or engaged in disorderly or disrespectful behavior in the presence of the court
Or interfered with the proceedings of the court
notes: Includes both civil (remedial) and criminal (punitive) contempt. Court has broad discretion. May be summarily punished if committed in the court's presence.

offense_class: Not a criminal offense (protective custody only)
elements: Person appeared intoxicated in a public place
Person was incapacitated or endangered themselves or others
notes: North Dakota decriminalized public intoxication. An intoxicated person may be taken into protective custody (not arrest) for up to 24 hours. No criminal penalty. Voluntary treatment encouraged.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor case); Class C Felony (felony case)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Defendant was required to appear in court at a specified time and place
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required
enhancements: Failure to appear in felony case (Class C Felony)
notes: Bail may be forfeited and bench warrant issued. Offense class matches the underlying charge level. Failure to appear is charged in addition to the original offense.

statute_title: Falsely Reporting a Crime or Emergency
offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly gave false information to a law enforcement officer
Regarding the commission of a crime or emergency
With the purpose of inducing a response
enhancements: False report causing emergency response or evacuation
notes: Includes false 911 calls, false bomb threats, and fabricated crime reports. May be charged as a felony if it results in injury or significant emergency response costs.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant threatened to commit any crime of violence
Or threatened to cause a catastrophe
With intent to place another person in fear for their safety
Or to cause evacuation of a building, public place, or transportation facility
enhancements: Threat involving weapon of mass destruction
Threat against school or public building
notes: North Dakota uses 'terrorizing' rather than 'criminal threat.' Includes bomb threats and threats against schools or public buildings. Need not have intent to carry out the threat.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (false swearing); Class C Felony (perjury in official proceeding)
elements: Defendant made a false statement under oath or affirmation
In an official proceeding
The statement was material to the issue or point in question
Defendant knew the statement was false
notes: False swearing (§ 12.1-11-02) is a lesser offense for false statements outside official proceedings. Corroboration or documentary proof typically required.

offense_class: Class C Felony
elements: Defendant offered, gave, or agreed to give a benefit
To a public servant
With intent to influence the public servant's official action
enhancements: Bribery of a judge or juror
notes: Both the giver and receiver of the bribe may be charged. Public servant includes elected officials, government employees, and jurors.

offense_class: Class C Felony (from felony detention); Class A Misdemeanor (from misdemeanor detention)
elements: Defendant was in official custody
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape from such custody
enhancements: Use of force or threat of force
notes: Official custody includes imprisonment, detention facility, and transport by law enforcement. Sentence for escape runs consecutive to original sentence.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general cruelty); Class C Felony (aggravated)
elements: Defendant willfully subjected an animal to unjustifiable physical pain, suffering, or death
Or deprived an animal of necessary sustenance, water, or shelter
notes: Aggravated cruelty involving torture, mutilation, or killing is a Class C Felony. Animal fighting is separately prohibited. Court may order forfeiture of animals.

offense_class: Varies — court may revoke probation and impose original sentence
penalty_max: Original sentence for the underlying offense
fine_max: Original fine for the underlying offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation with specific conditions
Defendant violated one or more conditions of probation
Violation was willful and without valid excuse
notes: Court has discretion to continue probation with modified conditions, extend probation, or revoke and impose incarceration. Hearing required before revocation. Burden of proof is preponderance of the evidence.

offense_class: Varies — Parole Board may revoke parole
elements: Defendant was released on parole with specific conditions
Defendant violated one or more conditions of parole
notes: Parole Board determines revocation. Revocation hearing required. May be returned to serve remainder of sentence. Technical violations may be treated differently than new criminal conduct.

statute_title: Criminal Liability for Conduct of Another (Aiding and Abetting)
offense_class: Same as the principal offense
elements: Defendant intentionally aided, abetted, or advised another person
In planning or committing a criminal offense
With the intent to promote or facilitate the commission of the offense
notes: Aider and abettor is punished the same as the principal. Mere presence at the scene is insufficient. Must have intent to promote or facilitate the crime.

offense_class: One class below the target offense
penalty_max: Varies by class of the target offense
fine_max: Varies by class of the target offense
elements: Defendant intended to commit a specific offense
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward the commission of the offense
The conduct was strongly corroborative of the criminal intent
notes: Attempt is generally one class below the target offense. Exception: attempted murder is Class A Felony (one below Class AA). Abandonment is a defense if voluntary and complete.

offense_class: One class below the target offense
penalty_max: Varies by class of the target offense
fine_max: Varies by class of the target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to engage in conduct constituting a crime
Defendant or a co-conspirator committed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement
Defendant intended that the crime be committed
notes: Conspiracy is one class below the target offense. Requires at least one overt act. Renunciation is a defense if the defendant thwarted the success of the conspiracy.
